title: GTM Enablement Manager, Field Training & Readiness - Atlanta
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Temporal is rapidly scaling its field organization, and setting up every seller to succeed, from day one and well beyond, is critical to meeting and exceeding our most ambitious goals.

As a GTM Enablement Manager, Field Training & Readiness, you’ll be the face of enablement in front of our sales teams. You’ll lead the live sessions where new hires and tenured sellers build the skills and confidence to have great customer conversations: bootcamp modules, workshops, role plays, and ongoing skills sessions. You’ll work from a defined track and a curriculum built with the enablement team, and you’ll bring it to life with your stories, your energy, and your read of the room.

If you’re energized by being in front of a room, believe training should be memorable and behavior-changing rather than a slide-reading exercise, and want to partner closely with the sales and BDR teams on the ground, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Deliver training that sticks. Lead a regular cadence of live, interactive sessions for Account Executives and BDRs and other customer-facing roles, including new hire cohorts, skills workshops, and role plays. Your sessions are built around practice, not presentation.

- Own your delivery track. Take ownership of a defined slate of programs and a delivery calendar. You’ll work from a curriculum built with the broader enablement team and make it your own through storytelling, real examples, and adapting on the fly. You’ll also flag what’s working and what isn’t so the content keeps getting better.

- Partner with the field. Stay close to the sales and BDR teams in Atlanta and beyond. Show up in team meetings, run role-play and call-practice reinforcement with managers, and bring what you hear (what’s resonating, where reps are stuck) back to the enablement team.

- Bring in the experts. You won’t be the expert on everything, and you don’t need to be. You’ll deliver the fundamentals with confidence and know when to pull in an AE, SA, or product expert to take a session deeper.

- Close the loop. Gather feedback and simple leading indicators (participation, skill demonstration, manager input) after every session and use them to iterate.

- Pitch in on the work behind the work. Scheduling, session prep, LMS updates, and content upkeep are shared across the team. You’ll own your share.

- Flex where the impact is. The core of this role is training delivery. As the team and the field grow, there will be room to expand into onboarding, BDR enablement, and broader field readiness.

WHO YOU ARE (NEED TO HAVES)

- Location: Atlanta metro area, or willingness to relocate. This role involves in-person collaboration with our sales and BDR teams, with a strong preference for 1-2 days a week in the office. In-person attendance is required for biweekly bootcamp delivery.

- You’re a natural facilitator. You come alive in front of a room. You’re outgoing, personable, and engaging; you use stories to make concepts real, and you can hold a room’s attention for hours. Your strength is how you facilitate, not just how you present: you read the audience, draw people in, and adapt on the fly. People leave your sessions feeling equipped, not talked at.

- You have a credible foundation in sales or enablement. You come from one of two places: you’ve spent 2+ years in a sales role (AE or BDR/SDR management) and want to move into enablement, or you’ve spent 5+ years delivering sales training or enablement at a comparable company or level. Either way, sellers listen to you because you understand their reality and speak their language.

- You earn credibility with humility. You know you aren’t the expert in our product or our customers. You build trust by being curious, prepared, and honest about what you know, and by bringing the right people into the room when it matters.

ABOUT FORESIGHT DIAGNOSTICS (A wholly-owned subsidiary of Natera)

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. 

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us. 

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our software portfolio spans bioinformatics pipelines, reagent QC systems, liquid handling automation, LIMS/LIS integrations, and NGS analysis tools. Each component carries regulatory obligations under IEC 62304 and ISO 13485, and each needs to be verified and validated with the rigor that clinical diagnostics demands.

This is a senior individual contributor role with real ownership - you'll set the V&V strategy across device software, manage the cadence and prioritization of testing activities, and serve as the quality and engineering bridge between bioinformatics, software, and lab teams. The candidate must bring genuine bioinformatics or computational biology experience: this isn't a role where you can learn the domain on the job.

 

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

You'll own verification and validation activities across Foresight's software portfolio - working closely with bioinformaticians, software engineers, and clinical laboratory teams to ensure every system is tested thoroughly and documented completely. In practice, that means: 

•

• Aligning all software testing processes with IEC 62304 and ISO 13485 design control requirements, and ensuring the team operates consistently within that framework.

• Overseeing V&V activities for pipeline software, lab automation methods, reagent QC software, LIMS/LIS tools, and select laboratory instruments.

• Designing and executing software verification tests for NGS bioinformatics pipelines - including tests for end-to-end analysis workflows and individual NGS algorithms.

• Developing and maintaining test templates, test protocols, and IEC 62304-aligned test cases that are clear, complete, and audit-ready.

• Reviewing executed test cases, assessing variances, and collaborating with the Quality Assurance team to resolve and document findings appropriately.

• Approving test reports and ensuring full documentation compliance under design controls.

• Establishing and maintaining V&V traceability across device software, lab automation tools, and lab instruments - including oversight of software traceability matrices across all device software components.

• Managing the cadence, prioritization, and execution of V&V activities across concurrent programs.

• Traveling to the Foresight lab in Boulder, CO on a regular basis to support testing activities, lab integration work, and cross-functional collaboration.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Required

• 4+ years conducting and overseeing software verification and validation activities for regulated medical device software (510(k) and/or PMA pathways).

• 3+ years designing and executing verification tests specifically for NGS bioinformatics pipelines - including NGS analysis workflows and individual algorithm testing.

• 2+ years of testing experience in cloud environments (AWS or GCP).

• Direct working knowledge of ISO 13485 and IEC 62304 design

title: PPC Marketing Specialist
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
